text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (ICTY) in the Hague invites Croatian Defence Minister Gojko Susak and his Bosnian counterpart Ante Jelavic, also a Croat, to testify in the case of indicted war criminal Bosnian Croat militia General Tihomil Blaskic.

- Arbitration decision over the disputed northern town of Brcko opens Bosnia's northern gate and will surely speed up economic recovery of Moslem-Croat Federation, president of the state arbitration commission Ejup Ganic says.

- If the arbitration decision for the town of Brcko is fully implemented, the town could become the nucleus of Bosnia's reintegration, a panel discussion held by Bosnia's opposition parties concludes.
- State authorities should step up control of imported goods to effectively collect custom taxes and other duties, Bosnian and Croatian trade unions agree at a meeting.
- Co-chairman of Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic met representatives of European aircraft producer Airbus to discuss purchasing aircraft for Bosnian commercial fleet.

- Report by London-based International Crisis Group says Croat police and extremists were to blame for violence last week in Mostar and calls on international police and NATO-led force to examine their ineffective response to the incident.

- By agreeing to single central bank for Bosnia, Serbs and Croats would be recognising the country itself. Raising tensions on the street is a last attempt to delay such a recognition, commentary says.

- A local policeman was killed on Saturday in an armed robbery of a petrol station near central town of Zenica. The other policeman managed to overpower and detain one of the perpetrators, an Italian citizen, Karlo Mazoni, who is now being questioned, a county interior minister official says. A U.S. and a Belgian citizen were also involved in the robbery.
